title: Hollow-Aerated Uruguayan Dough Bowl
description: A fun and tasty Uruguayan dish featuring a long-fermentation dough and a crunchy pickle topping, served in a traditional Korean brass bowl.

ingredients.name: Long-fermentation dough (see notes)
ingredients.notes: Use store-bought or make your own using flour, water, salt, and a starter culture.

ingredients.name: Chopped fresh parsley
ingredients.notes: Add some color and freshness to the dish.

ingredients.name: Red onion
ingredients.notes: Thinly slice and caramelize for added sweetness.

ingredients.name: Garlic
ingredients.notes: Minced and saut1ed for depth of flavor.

instructions: Roll out the dough to a thickness of about 1/4 inch (6 mm).
Use a cookie cutter or a knife to create fun shapes from the dough.
Place the dough shapes on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper.
Drizzle with vegetable oil and sprinkle with salt.
Bake in the preheated oven for 15 minutes, or until lightly browned.
While the dough is baking, caramelize the red onion and saut1e the garlic in a pan with a little bit of oil until softened.
Once the dough is done, let it cool for a few minutes before filling with pickle slices, chopped parsley, and caramelized onion.
Note: this recipe is for refrigerator pickling/preserving only — store in the refrigerator and consume within 1 week. Do not water-bath can without an acid (vinegar or lemon juice).
